queue.title: Found by today's fix: in its first moment a window tells a connected program 'there is no window'. What it should say is a ruling for the hub.
The sound chip's interrupt signal should last one line, not until taken. It changes what a real driver hears, so card d-51 asks whether you want to listen first.
From aeon: a watch never catches the sound chip reading an address. The warning half is landed and aeon is told; the full fix needs a contract change and a ruling later.
Sweep wave 1: both measured fixes landed today. Left: two look-at-it questions for you (how an unreadable save is shown; which rule the two address boxes share).
On bank-switching games, an address no longer names one byte over time, and nothing shows which bank was live beside a symbol, a watch hit or a profiler line.
Three of your ten remain: the clutter, the stacked tab strips, and dragging panels to any side. All three are takeable now -- I had wrongly parked them as things the rebuild would fix.

queue.blockedBy: one more drop attempt from you
queue.title: Three of four ways to open a ROM work. Dragging a file in does not, and it is not our bug -- the window library has no file drops on your desktop type. It is forced onto the older one now; try it.

queue.blockedBy: your look at the write-up first
queue.title: You liked the old command palette and this one has no easy way in. You get a written comparison of what the old one did before anyone spends on rebuilding it.
Unblocked now B is gone: the other panels follow the shared-card shape. Two for your eyes: the tab opening straight on its numbers, and how it clips in a narrow panel.
The reason I keep asking you to look at panels instead of reading them myself: the window can report its top bar to a connected program but not any panel.

The plane picture may redraw on data it never uses, and when it really does change every frame it is drawn the slow way. Not your lag. The old title said it redraws when nothing changed; re-derived at dispatch, that was wrong.
Nudging individual effect numbers is now buildable. Two constraints: only some fields have a reader at runtime, and the memory it needs is absent in a release build while the entry point resolves.
